methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
MightyFly is a Series A–stage drone and autonomous systems company founded by Manal Habib. The company has raised $10M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of 8 private companies in the Drones & Autonomous sector, including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro. No public comparables exist in this narrow subsector.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and forms the basis for valuation. Using total capital raised ($10M) as a proxy for post-money valuation at Series A, a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $20M. The Peer-Median method is not applicable; while 7 same-sector peers exist, insufficient overlap emerges when filtering by stage, adjacency, or valuation tier—fewer than the three datapoints required for reliable median calculation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $17M to $23M, with a median of $20M. This range reflects reasonable sensitivity around the stage-progression methodology, accounting for variance in how early-stage step-ups are marked in practice. The primary uncertainty is the absence of comparable Series A financings within Drones & Autonomous. A more granular range would require additional same-stage transaction data or public market signals to anchor the peer median method.
